title: Feel
subtitle: 本課涵蓋兩個核心義項：
description: 本課涵蓋兩個核心義項：

words.note: 當 feel 表示實際經歷某種情緒、身體狀態或感受時很自然。
words.example: Many people experience anxiety before an interview.
words.exampleZh: 很多人在面試前會感到焦慮。

exercises.original: Many people feel anxiety before an important interview.
exercises.zh: 很多人在重要面試前會感到焦慮。
exercises.upgrade: Many people experience anxiety before an important interview.

options.explanation: anxiety 是一種真正經歷到的情緒狀態。
通常表示察覺外在或隱約情況，不如 experience 適合明確情緒。
偏察覺，不是經歷情緒本身。
常用於直覺，不是這種已存在的焦慮狀態。

exercises.original: Some patients feel mild dizziness after the treatment.
exercises.zh: 一些病人在治療後會感到輕微頭暈。
exercises.upgrade: Some patients experience mild dizziness after the treatment.

options.explanation: 醫療語境中，症狀常用 experience dizziness/pain/nausea。
較像醫護人員發現症狀。
可感受到，但搭配不如 experience 自然。
表示注意到，不強調身體實際經歷。

exercises.original: She felt a strong sense of relief when the results arrived.
exercises.zh: 結果公布時，她感到強烈的鬆一口氣。
exercises.upgrade: She experienced a strong sense of relief when the results arrived.

options.explanation: relief 是她實際經歷的情緒。
更像察覺某種氣氛或情況。
只表示注意到感受，不如 experienced 直接。

words.note: 表示透過直覺、感官或細微線索感受到某事。
words.example: She sensed that something was wrong.
words.exampleZh: 她感覺到有些事情不對勁。

exercises.original: She felt that something was wrong even though nobody said anything.
exercises.zh: 雖然沒有人說話，她仍感覺到有些事情不對勁。
exercises.upgrade: She sensed that something was wrong.

options.explanation: 沒有直接證據但有直覺，最典型。
通常需要某種可觀察訊號。
不是在經歷一種情緒或症狀。
太確定，原句只是隱約感覺。

exercises.original: He felt tension in the room before anyone spoke.
exercises.zh: 任何人開口前，他已察覺房間裡的緊張氣氛。
exercises.upgrade: He sensed tension in the room.

options.explanation: tension 是從氣氛中直覺察覺。
如果說他本人感到緊張才更適合。
可成立，但較一般，不如 sense 有直覺感。

exercises.original: She could feel that the audience was losing interest.
exercises.zh: 她能感覺到觀眾正在失去興趣。
exercises.upgrade: She could sense that the audience was losing interest.

options.explanation: could 後用原形，且表示從細微反應中察覺。
也可能，但更客觀、分析化。
不是她在經歷觀眾的興趣下降。
也可，但通常更像已有可觀察證據。

words.note: 較正式，表示透過感官、理解或判斷意識到某事。
words.example: He perceived a change in her attitude.
words.exampleZh: 他察覺到她的態度有變化。

exercises.original: He felt a change in her attitude during the meeting.
exercises.zh: 會議期間，他察覺到她的態度有變化。
exercises.upgrade: He perceived a change in her attitude during the meeting.

options.explanation: 正式地表示注意並理解到態度改變。
也很自然，但更有直覺感。

exercises.original: Customers feel the new design as more modern and easier to use.
exercises.zh: 顧客認為新設計更現代、更容易使用。
exercises.upgrade: Customers perceive the new design as more modern and easier to use.

options.explanation: perceive something as... 是標準正式結構，表示如何看待。
通常不接 as + adjective 作此評價結構。

exercises.original: Researchers wanted to know how participants felt about the level of risk.
exercises.zh: 研究人員想知道參與者如何感知風險程度。
exercises.upgrade: Researchers wanted to know how participants perceived the level of risk.

options.explanation: 研究／心理語境中 perceived risk 很常見。
形容詞，表示觀察敏銳的。

words.note: 表示注意到某種細微變化、訊號、問題或存在。
words.example: She detected a slight smell of smoke.

exercises.original: She felt a faint smell of smoke near the door.
exercises.zh: 她在門邊察覺到一點煙味。
exercises.upgrade: She detected a faint smell of smoke near the door.

options.explanation: 微弱煙味是可感官偵測的具體訊號。

exercises.original: The technician could feel a slight vibration in the machine.
exercises.zh: 技術員能察覺機器有輕微震動。
exercises.upgrade: The technician could detect a slight vibration in the machine.

options.explanation: 技術檢查語境中，細微 vibration 很自然配 detect。
通常不形容 technician 經歷 machine vibration。
也可，但比 detect 少了「細微訊號」意味。

exercises.original: She felt a small change in temperature when the door opened.
exercises.zh: 門打開時，她察覺到輕微溫度變化。
exercises.upgrade: She detected a small change in temperature.

options.explanation: small change 表示細微、可感知差異。
如果重點是受到寒冷／炎熱影響可用，但這裡是辨認變化。
通常是直覺判斷，不是感官溫度變化。

words.note: 表示直覺上覺得某件事可能是真的。
words.example: I have a feeling that he already knows.
words.exampleZh: 我有種感覺，他已經知道了。

exercises.original: I feel that he already knows what happened.
exercises.zh: 我有種感覺，他已經知道發生甚麼事。
exercises.upgrade: I have a feeling that he already knows what happened.

options.explanation: 表示沒有完整證據的直覺判斷。
也可，但結構可改為 I sense that...，語氣稍更直接。

exercises.original: She felt that the meeting would not go as planned.
exercises.zh: 她有種感覺，會議不會按計劃進行。
exercises.upgrade: She had a feeling that the meeting would not go as planned.

options.explanation: 預感未來事情可能出問題。
也很接近，但通常像已察覺到某些跡象。
不是 feel 的過去式；正確是 felt。

exercises.original: I feel that we may have forgotten something important.
exercises.zh: 我有種感覺，我們可能忘了重要事情。
exercises.upgrade: I have a feeling that we may have forgotten something important.

options.explanation: may have 表示不確定直覺。
通常需要冠詞：have a feeling。

words.note: 表示知道或注意到某個狀況、感覺或變化。
words.example: She became aware of a dull pain in her shoulder.
words.exampleZh: 她開始察覺到肩膀有隱隱作痛。

exercises.original: She began to feel a dull pain in her shoulder.
exercises.zh: 她開始察覺肩膀有隱隱作痛。
exercises.upgrade: She began to be aware of a dull pain in her shoulder.

options.explanation: 重點是開始注意到一個逐漸出現的感覺。
也自然，但更直接說她有這個疼痛症狀。
也可，但不如 aware of 平穩中性。

exercises.original: He could feel people watching him as he entered the room.
exercises.zh: 他進房間時意識到有人在看他。
exercises.upgrade: He was aware of people watching him as he entered the room.

options.explanation: 表示他注意到這個情況。

exercises.original: She felt the change in mood almost immediately.
exercises.zh: 她幾乎立即意識到氣氛改變。
exercises.upgrade: She became aware of the change in mood almost immediately.

options.explanation: 強調注意到／意識到變化。
如果她本人情緒變化才更合適。

words.note: 當名詞 feel 指一個地方、活動或場合給人的整體氣氛時非常接近。
words.example: The café has a relaxed atmosphere.
words.exampleZh: 這間咖啡店有輕鬆的氣氛。

exercises.original: The café has a relaxed feel that makes people want to stay.
exercises.zh: 這間咖啡店有輕鬆的氣氛，讓人想留下來。
exercises.upgrade: The café has a relaxed atmosphere.

options.explanation: 最中性、廣泛地表示場所整體氣氛。
也很自然，更強調燈光、聲音、裝潢等環境感。
表示整體環境條件，不等於感覺上的氣氛。

exercises.original: The restaurant has a warm, welcoming feel.
exercises.zh: 這間餐廳有溫暖而友善的氣氛。
exercises.upgrade: The restaurant has a warm, welcoming atmosphere.

options.explanation: warm, welcoming 是典型場所氣氛描述。
也非常自然，尤其重視環境設計時。
表示獨特特色，而不是純氣氛。

exercises.original: The office has a very formal feel.
exercises.zh: 辦公室有非常正式的氣氛。
exercises.upgrade: The office has a very formal atmosphere.

options.explanation: 也可，但常更多用於美感／環境設計。
通常更像當下情緒狀態。
太口語，和 very formal 語域略衝突。

words.note: 表示一個地方由燈光、聲音、裝潢和整體環境形成的感覺。
words.example: Soft lighting creates a warm ambience.
words.exampleZh: 柔和燈光營造出溫暖氛圍。

exercises.original: Soft lighting gives the restaurant a warm feel.
exercises.zh: 柔和燈光令餐廳有溫暖氛圍。
exercises.upgrade: Soft lighting gives the restaurant a warm ambience.

options.explanation: lighting 直接影響環境感受，是 ambience 的典型語境。

exercises.original: The hotel has a luxurious feel created by music, lighting, and interior design.
exercises.zh: 音樂、燈光和室內設計營造出酒店奢華氛圍。
exercises.upgrade: The hotel has a luxurious ambience.

options.explanation: music + lighting + interior design 是最強線索。
強調獨特特色，不完全等於環境氣氛。

exercises.original: The candles created a calm feel in the room.
exercises.zh: 蠟燭在房間裡營造出平靜氛圍。
exercises.upgrade: The candles created a calm ambience in the room.

options.explanation: 燈光／裝飾帶來的場所感覺很適合 ambience。
也可，若重點是情緒基調。

words.note: 表示一個地方、作品或場合傳達出的情緒基調。
words.example: The music created a calm mood.
words.exampleZh: 音樂營造出平靜的氣氛。

exercises.original: The music gives the scene a calm feel.
exercises.zh: 音樂令場景帶有平靜的情緒氣氛。
exercises.upgrade: The music gives the scene a calm mood.

options.explanation: 音樂營造情緒基調，最自然。
形容詞，通常表示情緒多變／陰鬱。

exercises.original: The dark colours create a serious feel in the painting.
exercises.zh: 深色令畫作呈現嚴肅的情緒基調。
exercises.upgrade: The dark colours create a serious mood in the painting.

options.explanation: 藝術作品中的情緒基調很適合 mood。
也可能，但 mood 更聚焦情感色彩。

exercises.original: The opening scene establishes an uneasy feel.
exercises.zh: 開場建立了一種不安的氣氛。
exercises.upgrade: The opening scene establishes an uneasy mood.

options.explanation: 電影／故事場景建立情緒基調，是標準用法。

words.note: 較口語，表示一個地方、人或活動給人的整體感覺。
words.example: The neighbourhood has a friendly vibe.
words.exampleZh: 這個社區有親切友善的氛圍。

exercises.original: The neighbourhood has a friendly feel.
exercises.zh: 這個社區有親切友善的氛圍。
exercises.upgrade: The neighbourhood has a friendly vibe.

options.explanation: 現代口語中很自然地描述地方整體感覺。
也很自然，但較中性正式。
口語動詞／分詞，不能作此名詞。

exercises.original: The event had a relaxed, informal feel.
exercises.zh: 活動有輕鬆、非正式的氛圍。
exercises.upgrade: The event had a relaxed, informal vibe.

options.explanation: relaxed + informal 很符合口語 vibe。

exercises.original: The studio has a creative feel that appeals to young artists.
exercises.zh: 這間工作室有很有創意的氛圍，吸引年輕藝術家。
exercises.upgrade: The studio has a creative vibe.

options.explanation: creative vibe 是非常自然現代搭配。
也接近，但表示獨特特色，而不是單純氣氛。
不如 vibe 適合 creative studio 的整體感覺。
通常可說 good vibes，但本句結構需要單數 a ... vibe。

words.note: 當 feel 指一個地方、設計或空間的獨特整體印象時可接近。
words.example: The old wooden beams give the room character.
words.exampleZh: 舊木樑令房間很有特色。

exercises.original: The old wooden beams give the room a distinctive feel.
exercises.zh: 舊木樑令房間具有獨特特色。
exercises.upgrade: The old wooden beams give the room character.

options.explanation: 建築細節令空間有獨特、可辨識特色。
也可有氣氛，但沒有突出獨特性。
形容詞／名詞「特徵」，句法不同。

exercises.original: The handmade furniture gives the café a unique feel.
exercises.zh: 手工家具令咖啡店很有獨特風格。
exercises.upgrade: The handmade furniture gives the café character.

options.explanation: handmade furniture 建立場所獨特特色。
也可，但更偏整體環境氛圍。
複數意思通常是人物／文字符號。

exercises.original: The renovation kept the building's traditional feel.
exercises.zh: 翻新保留了建築的傳統特色。
exercises.upgrade: The renovation kept the building's traditional character.

options.explanation: building's traditional character 是標準搭配，表示長期獨特風格。
比較像人在空間中的感受。

falseSynonyms.zh: 覺得 ≠ 一定是 feel think 通常來自思考／判斷； feel 可以來自情緒、直覺或感官。
觸摸 ≠ 所有 feel feel 可以表示用手觸摸，但本課不處理這個義項。
情緒 ≠ 動詞「感到」 emotion 是名詞，指情緒本身。
感覺 ≠ 所有 feel sensation 常指具體身體感覺，例如 heat, pressure, pain。
意見 ≠ 感覺 "I feel that..." 有時表示意見，但 opinion 本身不是 feel 的一般同義詞。
環境 ≠ 氛圍 environment 是整體環境條件；atmosphere / ambience 才是「感覺上的氛圍」。
詞形陷阱 - feel = 動詞／名詞 - feeling = 感覺、情緒 - felt = feel 的過去式／過去分詞
詞形不同 - sense = 感覺到／感官 - sensation = 感覺 - sensitive = 敏感的
